title: Break the fewest walls
statement:
A grid has open cells '.' and wall cells '#'. You start in the top-left cell and want to reach the bottom-right cell, moving up, down, left or right one cell at a time and never leaving the grid. Walking into an open cell is free; walking into a wall cell means breaking that wall, which costs 1 (a broken wall stays open). Print the smallest number of walls you must break to reach the bottom-right cell.

Input: the first line holds r and c (1 <= r, c <= 600). Each of the next r lines holds c characters, each '.' or '#'. The top-left and bottom-right cells are always '.'.

Output: one line with the minimum number of walls to break.

Example
Input:
4 5
..#..
####.
...#.
.#...
Output:
1
(Break the '#' in the top row, then walk right to the last column and down it. Without breaking a wall you cannot leave the first two cells.)
